brique._comment: Engine-native Matter family capacity. kind/wrapper/rel_ctx/lang do not apply here.

objective.name: matter.create
objective.description: Create one new matter in the local context and optionally seed its brique-managed payload.

#root.role: Build a new matter descriptor, create its local storage, and register the new matter in the runtime catalog.

matter_id._comment: Optional. Name for the new matter within the current context. Auto-generated by the engine when absent.

matter._comment: Optional opaque matter descriptor seed. Minimal sections are ensured by the engine when absent.

payload._comment: Optional initial substance. Allowed only when the resulting matter is in brique substance mode. Strings become raw bytes; other values are JSON-marshaled. How matter.read later serializes this content (plain string vs base64) is controlled separately by brique.substance_type inside the 'matter' descriptor seed above ('text', the default, or 'binary') — this payload param itself carries no encoding declaration, so set matter.brique.substance_type explicitly at create time if the payload is arbitrary binary data, or matter.read will hand it back as an unencoded string.

created._comment: The concrete created matter is the one designated or generated for params.matter_id in the current context.

effects.matter_descriptor: A new local matter.json is written.
effects.matter_substance: A brique-managed data.bin may be created when the selected substance mode allows payload materialization.
effects.catalog: The local matter catalog gains a new entry.

transformation_contract.morphing: A caller-supplied matter definition becomes a new committed local matter, optionally with initial brique-managed substance, and gains an explicit catalog identity.
invariants: If matter_id is omitted, the capacity generates a fresh local matter identifier.
When the resulting matter uses brique substance mode, the create path always leaves a local data.bin file present, either populated from payload or empty.
When the resulting matter does not use brique substance mode, payload materialization is refused.
success: On success, matter.create returns ok=true, the concrete matter_id, and the committed revision stored in matter.json.
Successful creation writes matter.json, updates the runtime catalog, and may seed brique-managed substance bytes when payload is allowed.
failure: The capacity refuses creation when the designated or generated matter_id already exists in the runtime catalog.
The capacity fails when payload or matter metadata cannot be marshaled or committed to disk.
The capacity refuses payload writes when the supplied matter metadata resolves to a non-brique substance mode.
notes: The created matter identity is local to the current context.
The matter document itself remains opaque apart from minimal brique normalization and revision stamping.
